stem:
Isha has the sorted scores $3$, $5$, $8$, $9$, $11$ (median $8$). She inserts the value $2$ into the list.

How does the median change?

options.text: Say the median moves down after inserting $2$, skipping that the data must stay sorted and the new middle position(s) must be checked.
Say that the new median is what creates the inserted value $2$, instead of the insertion changing the middle.
After inserting $2$, the sorted list is $2$, $3$, $5$, $8$, $9$, $11$; the middle pair is $5$ and $8$, so the median moves downward from $8$.
Use the same middle-tracking rule to decide how the mean changes when $2$ is inserted.

teacher.key_rationale: Inserting a value below the old median and re-finding the middle moves the median down: here to the average of $5$ and $8$. Skipping sort/middle checks, reversing median and insert, or swapping mean for median all miss that hinge.
